articles.title: Overwrote a secret by mistake? Writing, pulling and rolling back keys
articles.excerpt: This is part 4 of the series "dotvault, Start to Finish: One Command from Your Laptop to CI, Your Team, and Your AI Agents." dotvault will be released free of charge when this series ends. Paste the s…
articles.body: This is part 4 of the series "dotvault, Start to Finish: One Command from Your Laptop to CI, Your Team, and Your AI Agents." dotvault will be released free of charge when this series ends. Paste the staging DATABASE_URL over the dev one by mistake, and with a plain .env the old value is gone the moment you save. In dotvault it is not: one command, dotvault rollback , brings it back. Writing a key never destroys the previous value. Each write is a new version: DATABASE_URL v1, then v2. dotvault versions DATABASE_URL lists them newest first with a timestamp, the writer's ID and a hash of the value. dotvault rollback DATABASE_URL --to 1 restores v1, and the restore itself is recorded as v3, so v2 stays in the history. Deleting a key removes its current value and keeps the history too.

articles.title: Why Most Backtests Lie — and the 7 Checks That Catch Them
articles.excerpt: A beautiful backtest is the easiest thing in trading to fake — usually by accident. Here are the seven ways backtests mislead, and the check that catches each one. A backtest is a story about the past…
articles.body: A beautiful backtest is the easiest thing in trading to fake — usually by accident. Here are the seven ways backtests mislead, and the check that catches each one. A backtest is a story about the past, told by someone who already knows how it ends. That is why it lies so well — usually without anyone intending to lie. Every trader has lived the same disappointment: a strategy that looked unstoppable in testing falls apart the moment real money touches it. The usual explanation is “the market changed.” Sometimes that is true. More often, the backtest was never evidence in the first place. It was a fitting exercise that found noise and dressed it as signal. Here are the seven ways backtests mislead, and the check that catches each one. 1.

articles.title: Data-Driven API Runs: CSV Tables in a Cloud Client vs Plain Spec Files
articles.excerpt: Quick answer Data-driven testing means running the same request and assertion logic against many input rows rather than copying a test for each case. Cloud clients popularized this with a CSV table at…
articles.body: Quick answer Data-driven testing means running the same request and assertion logic against many input rows rather than copying a test for each case. Cloud clients popularized this with a CSV table attached to a request, but that table lives inside a proprietary collection and is hard to review or run in CI. Plain spec files do the same job with a portable data file and a small runner, which keeps the cases in version control alongside the contract. If you reach for a CSV, first ask whether the data belongs in the OpenAPI examples and a parameterized test; the answer is usually yes, and you avoid locking the cases into one GUI.

articles.title: To plan or not to plan: the Terraform file that leaked every password we had
articles.excerpt: Committing an API key to a repo is the nightmare every developer has had at least once. Most of us have a scanner, a hook and a .gitignore that are supposed to make it impossible. I never thought I wo…
articles.body: Committing an API key to a repo is the nightmare every developer has had at least once. Most of us have a scanner, a hook and a .gitignore that are supposed to make it impossible. I never thought I would be writing this post. Then a Terraform plan file showed up in our git history. A Terraform plan file is a zip archive. It does not care what you name it. Our .gitignore cared. Our secret scanner cared. Both were looking for *.tfplan , tfplan and plan , and the file that was committed was called out . I ran it. I know the convention. The command I meant to type was terraform plan -out=tfplan . The command I typed was terraform plan -out=out . Terraform does not care. The file went in with the next git add . . The one small mercy: the repository is private.

articles.title: Using OpenAPI links to Connect a Response to the Next Request
articles.excerpt: Quick answer OpenAPI links let you declare that a value in one response is meant to be used in a later request, connecting operations into a flow instead of leaving them as a flat list. A link can map…
articles.body: Quick answer OpenAPI links let you declare that a value in one response is meant to be used in a later request, connecting operations into a flow instead of leaving them as a flat list. A link can map a returned id into a path or query parameter on the next call, so clients and generated code can follow the workflow without hardcoding field names. Most teams ignore links and hand-write the same extraction in every client; the ones that use them get discoverable, machine-readable workflows. Start with one obvious pair, such as create order then retrieve it by the returned id, and add operation references so the link is unambiguous. What a link actually declares A link lives on a response and points at another operation, describing how to build the next request from runtime data.

articles.title: Time Zones Are Hard: Building a Converter with Intl.DateTimeFormat (DST Gaps, Folds and 5:45 Offsets)
articles.excerpt: Remote teams, international calls and API logs share one problem: a time that is perfectly clear in one city is ambiguous everywhere else. "Let's meet at 3 pm" is not a time until it has a zone attach…
articles.body: Remote teams, international calls and API logs share one problem: a time that is perfectly clear in one city is ambiguous everywhere else. "Let's meet at 3 pm" is not a time until it has a zone attached. We built a free Time Zone Converter to deal with this. You enter a date and time in any of 40 IANA time zones , and it shows the same moment in up to 8 other zones at once , each with its UTC offset and daylight-saving abbreviation. There's no server call and no sign-up. The browser's built-in Intl.DateTimeFormat does the work. This post covers why that API is enough for most of the job, and which edge cases are worth knowing even if you never use our tool.

articles.body: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space.
